<!-- CONCLUSION -->

# Background and question

This is the third audit of its kind. `../Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus/are_these_real.qmd`
and `../north_shore_virus/are_these_real.qmd` showed that the 16,699 Cheeloo
Jingmen-like virus contigs and all but 9 of the 10,390 North shore virus contigs were
tick genomic repeats. In both cases a tick repeat sits at the end of the viral reference
records. Those contigs are now re-assigned to Ixodida (`metadata/contig_reassignments.tsv`)
and are **not** repeated here.

This document covers **every other contig whose LCA is a virus**. For each one, it asks
whether the contig is:

1. **genuine virus**, i.e. viral nucleic acid carried through the DNA extraction (or,
   for phages, phage or prophage DNA);
2. an **endogenous viral element (EVE)**, i.e. viral coding sequence integrated in a
   host genome and flanked by host DNA;
3. a **misclassified genomic element**, such as:
   - a tick (or other host) repeat, including a SINE, carried in a viral reference
     record;
   - a cellular gene with a viral homologue; or
4. **technical sequence**, i.e. library adapters shared by our contigs and the
   reference records.

Lines of evidence used:

- contig length vs viral-hit length, and non-viral co-hits in the original BLAST;
- a competitive protein-level search (DIAMOND blastx against viral **and** cellular
  proteins);
- where the nucleotide hits fall on the reference records (inside a CDS or not), and
  whether they pile up on one narrow window;
- adapter content of those windows and of our contigs;
- for each recurring element:
  - copy number;
  - flank diversity;
  - tick-genus distribution;
  - a tRNA B-box motif;
  - an NCBI search for the element in cellular genomes;
- for protein-supported contigs: what flanks the viral ORF, and whether the reading
  frame is intact.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Set-up: paths, tool locations and plotting helpers"
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

ROOT <- "/data/hb-austick/work/AlexG_data/Barker_ticks/microbe_analysis/old_analysis"
OV   <- file.path(ROOT, "extracting_pathogens/other_viral_taxa")
W    <- file.path(OV, "are_these_real")           # all intermediate files land here
dir.create(file.path(W, "ncbi"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Bash chunks inherit these. BLAST+, DIAMOND, cd-hit and python3 come from the
# base miniforge install; seqkit is the system copy.
Sys.setenv(ROOT = ROOT, OV = OV, W = W,
           PATH = paste("/data/hb-austick/work/miniforge3/bin", "/usr/bin",
                        Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep = ":"))

col_main <- "#014B87"   # CSIRO Ocean Blue
col_alt  <- "#E87721"   # CSIRO Orange
cat_cols <- c("genuine" = "#014B87", "genuine (prophage)" = "#6EC1E4",
              "EVE candidate" = "#E87721", "misclassified genomic" = "#78BE20",
              "technical artefact" = "#DF1995", "unverified" = "#BBBBBB")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                plot.title.position = "plot"))
rd <- function(f, ...) read.delim(file.path(W, f), check.names = FALSE, quote = "", ...)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

# Extraction

Upstream, every SPAdes contig was searched with `blastn` (megablast) against NCBI nt
(2025-05-04 snapshot), using `-max_target_seqs 10 -evalue 1e-5`, and an LCA was computed
per contig. `extract_other_viral_taxa.sh` is the North shore virus extraction script,
generalised from one taxid to a list. The list (`viral_taxids.tsv`) holds every taxon in
`results/taxonomy/taxon_lineage.tsv` with `superkingdom_group == Viruses`, except
Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus and North shore virus. The script writes, per sample:

- the contigs (`fasta/`);
- **all** BLAST hits of those contigs (`blast/`);
- the LCA rows (`lca_assignments.tsv`).

::: {.callout-note}
As before, `-max_target_seqs 10` means a **missing** non-viral hit is weak evidence, and
a **present** one is informative. The extraction streams every sample's BLAST file
(~460 GB; one is 160 GB), so it was run once, outside this document.
:::

```{bash}
#| label: show-extract
#| code-summary: "The extraction script (run once, outside this document)"
cat "$OV/extract_other_viral_taxa.sh"
echo; echo "---- log notes ----"; grep -E "NOTE|WARN" "$OV/extract.log" || echo none
```

```{bash}
#| label: step01
#| code-summary: "Step 01: per-contig nucleotide evidence (scripts/01_contig_evidence.py)"
cd "$OV"
[ -s "$W/contig_evidence.tsv" ] && [ "$W/contig_evidence.tsv" -nt lca_assignments.tsv ] ||
  python3 scripts/01_contig_evidence.py
sed -n '2,/^"""/p' scripts/01_contig_evidence.py | head -n -1
```

```{r}
#| label: overview
#| code-summary: "Contigs, samples and sequence per virus group"
vt <- rd("viral_taxa.tsv")
ce <- rd("contig_evidence.tsv")
summ <- read.delim(file.path(OV, "summary.tsv"))
cat(sprintf("%s samples, %s contigs, %s bp, %s BLAST hits, %d viral taxa\n", nrow(summ),
            fmt(sum(summ$n_contigs)), fmt(sum(summ$total_bp)), fmt(sum(summ$n_blast_hits)),
            sum(vt$n_contigs > 0)))
ce |> group_by(virus_group) |>
  summarise(taxa = n_distinct(lca_taxid), contigs = n(), samples = n_distinct(sample_id),
            Mb = round(sum(len) / 1e6, 2), median_len = median(len),
            median_viral_bp = median(viral_bp)) |>
  arrange(desc(contigs)) |> kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
                                  caption = "Viral-LCA contigs by virus group")
```

`bacteriophage` means the lineage runs through a phage or archaeal-virus clade
(*Caudoviricetes*, *Inoviridae*, *Microviridae*, …). `unresolved` means the LCA stopped
above family and outside those clades (*Viruses*, *Riboviria*, *Heunggongvirae*).

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-taxa

#| fig-width: 9
```

```{r}
ce |> summarise(median_viral_bp = median(viral_bp), median_len = median(len),
```

# Which contigs encode viral protein?

## A competitive protein search

A viral-only protein database would over-call viruses. Herpesvirus dUTPase, phage
integrases and many other viral proteins have cellular homologues. Each contig was
therefore searched with DIAMOND blastx (`--sensitive`, e ≤ 1e-5, 25 targets) against a
database that holds both:

| Component | Proteins | Group |
|---|---|---|
| RefSeq viral proteins | ~723,000 | virus |
| CDS translations of every viral record our contigs hit (most tick viruses are not in RefSeq) | see below | virus |
| UniProt Swiss-Prot | ~576,000 | by taxid: bacteria, vertebrate, arthropod, … |
| *Ixodes scapularis* proteome (GCF_016920785.2) | ~34,000 | tick |

A contig is **viral at the protein level** only if its best viral hit scores at least as
high as its best cellular hit.

```{bash}
#| label: step02-04
#| code-summary: "Steps 02-04: fetch hit records, build the protein database, DIAMOND blastx"
cd "$OV"
[ -s "$W/ncbi/hitrec.ft" ] || python3 scripts/02_fetch_hit_records.py
[ -s "$W/protdb.dmnd" ]    || python3 scripts/03_build_protein_db.py
[ -s "$W/protein_evidence.tsv" ] && [ "$W/protein_evidence.tsv" -nt "$W/diamond.tsv" ] ||
  python3 scripts/04_protein_evidence.py
echo "viral records hit: $(grep -c '^>Feature' $W/ncbi/hitrec.ft);  proteins from them: $(grep -c '^>' $W/ncbi/hitrec_prot.fa)"
cut -f2 "$W/protdb_groups.tsv" | tail -n +2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

```{r}
#| label: prot-calls
#| code-summary: "Protein call by virus group"
pe <- rd("protein_evidence.tsv")
cep <- ce |> mutate(id = paste0(sample, "|", contig)) |> left_join(pe, by = "id")
cep |> count(virus_group, prot_call) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prot_call, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(pct_viral = round(100 * viral / (viral + cellular + none), 1)) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Best protein hit: viral, cellular, or none")
cep |> filter(prot_call == "cellular") |> count(virus_group, cell_group) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = virus_group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))))) |>
  kable(caption = "Contigs whose best protein hit is cellular: which organism group wins")
```

# Where the nucleotide hits fall on the reference records

Each viral hit was placed on its reference record and tested against the record's CDS
annotation (GenBank feature tables). The search then looked for **hotspots** within each
record: the 300 bp window covered by the most distinct contigs. That window was set
aside and the search repeated. This is how both earlier audits found their elements, as
thousands of contigs stacked on 70–300 bp at one end of the records. A genuine virus
sampled by many contigs instead tiles the whole record.

```{bash}
#| label: step05
#| code-summary: "Step 05: hits on the references, hotspots (scripts/05_reference_hotspots.py)"
cd "$OV" && python3 scripts/05_reference_hotspots.py
```

```{r}
#| label: hotspots
#| code-summary: "The largest hotspots"
hs <- rd("hotspots.tsv")
hw <- rd("hotspot_windows.tsv")
hs <- hs |> mutate(hotspot = paste0(saccver, "#", peak)) |>
  left_join(select(hw, hotspot, element, adapter_bp), by = "hotspot")
cat(sprintf("%d hotspots (>= 10 contigs) on %d records, holding %s contig-hotspot memberships; %.1f%% of their hits fall outside any annotated CDS\n",
            nrow(hs), n_distinct(hs$saccver), fmt(sum(hs$n_contigs)),
            100 * (1 - weighted.mean(hs$frac_in_cds, hs$n_contigs))))
hs |> slice_max(n_contigs, n = 25) |>
  transmute(record = saccver, species = ssciname, window = paste0(start, "-", end),
            contigs = n_contigs, samples = n_samples, share, in_CDS = frac_in_cds,
            protein_viral = frac_prot_viral, hit_len = median_hit_len,
            element = ifelse(element == "adapter", "ADAPTER", element)) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "25 largest hotspots. share = hotspot contigs / all contigs hitting the record; in_CDS = fraction of hits inside an annotated CDS; protein_viral = fraction of hotspot contigs with viral protein support")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-depth
#| fig-cap: "Hit depth (distinct contigs per position) along the eight most-hit reference records. Shaded: annotated CDS. Every record shows a single tall spike outside the coding sequence."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9
hr <- rd("hits_ref.tsv")
top <- hr |> distinct(id, saccver, ssciname) |> count(saccver, ssciname) |> slice_max(n, n = 8)
ft <- readLines(file.path(W, "ncbi/hitrec.ft"))
cds <- list(); acc <- NA; key <- NA
for (l in ft) {
  if (startsWith(l, ">Feature")) { acc <- sub(".*\\|([^|]+)\\|.*", "\\1", l); key <- NA; next }
  a <- strsplit(l, "\t")[[1]]
  if (length(a) >= 3 && nzchar(a[3])) key <- a[3]
  if (acc %in% top$saccver && length(a) >= 2 && nzchar(a[1]) && identical(key, "CDS"))
    cds[[length(cds) + 1]] <- data.frame(saccver = acc,
      s = as.numeric(gsub("[<>]", "", a[1])), e = as.numeric(gsub("[<>]", "", a[2])))
}
cds <- bind_rows(cds) |> mutate(lo = pmin(s, e), hi = pmax(s, e))
dep <- hr |> filter(saccver %in% top$saccver) |> distinct(id, saccver, sstart, send) |>
  rowwise() |> reframe(saccver, pos = seq(sstart, send, by = 5)) |>
  count(saccver, pos, name = "contigs")
lab <- setNames(paste0(top$saccver, " ", top$ssciname, " (", fmt(top$n), " contigs)"), top$saccver)
ggplot(dep, aes(pos, contigs)) +
  geom_rect(data = cds, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = col_main, alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_col(width = 5, fill = col_main) +
  facet_wrap(~saccver, scales = "free", ncol = 2, labeller = as_labeller(lab)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Position on the reference record", y = "Distinct contigs") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{bash}
#| label: step06-07
#| code-summary: "Steps 06-07: classify contigs; characterise hotspot windows as elements"
cd "$OV"
python3 scripts/06_classify.py      # first pass: element step reads tick genus from here
python3 scripts/07_elements.py
python3 scripts/06_classify.py
```

```{r}
#| label: adapters
#| code-summary: "Hotspot windows that are adapter sequence"
ad <- hw |> filter(element == "adapter") |> left_join(select(hs, hotspot, ssciname, n_contigs, n_samples), by = "hotspot")
cat(sprintf("%d of %d hotspot windows are adapter / homopolymer sequence; they hold %s contig memberships across %d records\n",
            nrow(ad), nrow(hw), fmt(sum(ad$n_contigs)), n_distinct(sub("#.*", "", ad$hotspot))))
ad |> arrange(desc(n_contigs)) |> head(8) |>
  transmute(hotspot, species = ssciname, contigs = n_contigs,
            sequence = ifelse(nchar(sequence) > 110, paste0(substr(sequence, 1, 110), "…"), sequence)) |>
  kable(caption = "Largest adapter hotspots, with the window sequence")
```

```{r}
  summarise(contigs = n(), samples = n_distinct(sample_id), taxa = n_distinct(lca_name),
            median_len = median(len), median_adapter_bp = median(adapter_bp)) |> kable()
```

# Tick genomic elements in the reference records

The hotspot windows that are not adapter sequence were clustered into **elements** by
all-vs-all blastn. For each element, the longest window was used as a probe against
every viral-LCA contig to measure:

- copy number;
- flank diversity, i.e. the 150 bp either side of each copy, clustered at 90% with
  cd-hit-est;
- tick-genus distribution.

Each probe was also searched against the Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus and North shore
virus elements, and checked for a tRNA B-box (`GGTTCGANTCC`, either strand).

Finally, each probe, a subsequence of a **public** viral record, was sent to NCBI BLAST
(megablast, core_nt) **with viruses excluded**. A hit there is a cellular record that
carries the same sequence.

```{bash}
#| label: step08
#| code-summary: "Step 08: remote NCBI BLAST of the element probes, viruses excluded (cached)"
cd "$OV" && python3 scripts/08_remote_blast_elements.py
```

```{r}
#| label: elements
#| code-summary: "Elements: copies, flanks, genera, cellular hits"
el <- rd("elements.tsv")
rb <- rd("remote_blast.tsv")
rb1 <- rb |> group_by(element) |>
  summarise(cellular_hit = ifelse(first(rank) == 0, "none (megablast)",
              sprintf("%s (%s%% / %s bp)", first(title), first(pident), first(aln_len))))
el |> left_join(rb1, by = "element") |>
  transmute(element, `reference species` = ref_species, records = n_windows,
            `hotspot contigs` = hotspot_contigs, copies, `contigs w/ copy` = contigs_with_copy,
            `flank clusters (up)` = sprintf("%d / %d", up_clusters, up_flanks),
            `flank clusters (down)` = sprintf("%d / %d", down_clusters, down_flanks),
            genera, `B-box` = bbox, in_CDS = frac_in_cds, `similar to` = similar_to,
            `best non-viral NCBI hit` = cellular_hit) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "Elements. Flank clusters: 90% clusters / flanks; close to 1 cluster per flank = a different genomic context for every copy (interspersed repeat).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-elem-genus
#| fig-cap: "Copies of each element by tick genus (viral-LCA contigs only). Labels: samples with the element / samples of that genus with any viral-LCA contig."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
ec <- rd("element_copies.tsv")
gsz <- cv |> distinct(sample_id, tick_genus) |> count(tick_genus, name = "n_genus")
eg <- ec |> distinct(element, id) |>
  left_join(distinct(cv, id, sample_id, tick_genus), by = "id") |>
  group_by(element, tick_genus) |> summarise(copies = n(), samples = n_distinct(sample_id), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(gsz, by = "tick_genus")
ggplot(eg, aes(tick_genus, copies)) +
  geom_col(fill = col_main, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(samples, "/", n_genus)), vjust = -0.3, size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(element, levels = el$element), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Contigs carrying a copy") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: cellular

  arrange(desc(contigs)) |> kable(caption = "Cellular-gene contigs, by the group of the winning protein")
cv |> filter(class == "cellular gene") |> count(lca_name, cell_group, sort = TRUE, name = "contigs") |>
  head(15) |> kable(caption = "Taxa most often called from a cellular gene")
cv |> filter(class == "cellular gene", virus_group != "bacteriophage") |>
  mutate(cell_title = sub(" OS=.*", "", cell_title)) |>
  count(cell_group, cell_title, sort = TRUE, name = "contigs") |> head(15) |>
  kable(caption = "Most frequent winning cellular proteins (eukaryotic and unresolved viruses)")
```

# Endogenous viral elements

A contig is an **EVE candidate** if it encodes a viral protein (viral hit beats every
cellular hit, ≥ 90 bp) and, **outside** that viral region, either:

- carries a eukaryotic protein (≥ 150 bp of cellular blastx coverage not overlapping the
  viral HSPs, best cellular group tick, arthropod, vertebrate or other eukaryote); or
- has a eukaryotic nucleotide hit (≥ 50 bp not overlapping a viral hit).

That is, viral coding sequence joined to host sequence. Contigs with a viral ORF and
≥ 500 bp of sequence that has **no** evidence either way are listed separately
(`viral ORF + long flank`). They are weaker candidates, since the flank could be
non-coding viral sequence missing from the databases.

```{bash}
#| label: step09
#| code-summary: "Step 09: reading frames of protein-supported contigs (tblastn vs best viral protein)"
cd "$OV" && python3 scripts/09_reading_frames.py && wc -l < "$W/reading_frames.tsv"
```

```{r}
#| label: eve
#| code-summary: "EVE candidates"
rf <- rd("reading_frames.tsv")
eve <- cv |> filter(category == "EVE candidate") |> left_join(rf, by = "id")
eve |> count(class, lca_name, viral_family, sort = TRUE, name = "contigs") |>
  kable(caption = "EVE candidates by taxon")
eve |> filter(class == "EVE candidate (host flank)") |>
  transmute(id, tick_genus, taxon = lca_name, len, cov = kmer_cov,
            viral_protein = substr(viral_title, 1, 50), aa_id = viral_pident,
            viral_bp = viral_prot_bp, flank_group = ifelse(cell_group != "", cell_group, nonviral_groups),
            host_protein = substr(sub(" OS=.*", "", cell_title), 1, 45),
            stops, frames) |>
  arrange(taxon) |> kable(caption = "EVE candidates with host sequence beside the viral ORF")
```

## Taxon overrides

Three groups encode a viral protein but are not evidence of a virus in the tick, so their
protein-supported contigs are reclassified whatever their flanks:

- **Retroviridae** -> `endogenous retrovirus` (EVE candidate). The hits are vertebrate
  ERVs (Echidna ERV, possum and bower bird retroviruses), carried in blood-meal DNA.
- **Eupolintoviridae** -> `endogenous adintovirus` (EVE candidate). Adintoviruses are
  polinton-like elements integrated in host genomes.
- **Papillomaviridae at >= 95 % aa identity** -> `human papillomavirus contaminant`
  (technical artefact). Near-identical human HPV types are reagent or handling
  contamination.

```{r}
#| label: overrides
#| code-summary: "Contigs reclassified by taxon override"
cv |> filter(class %in% c("endogenous retrovirus", "endogenous adintovirus",
                          "human papillomavirus contaminant")) |>
  group_by(class, lca_name) |>
  summarise(contigs = n(), samples = n_distinct(sample_id),
            aa_identity = paste(range(round(viral_pident)), collapse = "-"),
            genera = paste(sort(unique(tick_genus)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(class, desc(contigs)) |> kable(caption = "Contigs reclassified by taxon override")
```

# Genuine viruses

```{r}
#| label: genuine
#| code-summary: "Protein-supported eukaryotic-virus contigs without host flanks"
md <- read.delim(file.path(ROOT, "metadata/sample_metadata.tsv"))
gen <- cv |> filter(class == "viral (protein-supported)") |> left_join(rf, by = "id")
gen |> group_by(lca_name, viral_family) |>
  summarise(contigs = n(), samples = n_distinct(sample_id), kb = round(sum(len) / 1e3, 1),
            median_cov = median(kmer_cov), aa_identity = paste(range(round(viral_pident)), collapse = "-"),
            with_stops = sum(stops > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            genera = paste(sort(unique(tick_genus)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(contigs)) |>
  kable(caption = "Eukaryotic and unresolved viral taxa with protein-supported, flank-free contigs")
```

```{r}
#| label: phage
#| code-summary: "Bacteriophages"
cv |> filter(virus_group == "bacteriophage") |> count(class, sort = TRUE, name = "contigs") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * contigs / sum(contigs), 1)) |> kable(caption = "Bacteriophage contigs by class")
```

<!-- GENUINE-TEXT -->

# Verdict for every taxon

The contig classes roll up into five categories:

| Category | Contig classes |
|---|---|
| genuine | viral (protein-supported); phage (protein-supported) |
| genuine (prophage) | phage protein beside a bacterial gene or hit |
| EVE candidate | EVE candidate (host flank); viral ORF + long flank; endogenous retrovirus; endogenous adintovirus |
| misclassified genomic | hotspot repeat; tick sequence (no protein, tick nt co-hit); cellular gene |
| technical artefact | adapter artefact; human papillomavirus contaminant |
| unverified | nucleotide-only hits, no protein, no repeat or host signal |

A taxon's verdict is its majority category. Genuine and EVE contigs are always listed
when present, even when artefacts dominate (as for North shore virus: 9 genuine contigs
among 10,390).

```{r}
#| label: fig-categories
#| fig-cap: "Contig categories for the 30 viral taxa with the most contigs."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
tv <- rd("taxon_verdicts.tsv")
cats <- names(cat_cols)
tv |> slice_max(n_contigs, n = 30, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(cats), names_to = "category", values_to = "contigs") |>
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = rev(cats))) |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(name, n_contigs), contigs, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cat_cols, breaks = cats, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Contigs") + theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: all-totals
#| code-summary: "Totals over all taxa"
cv |> count(category, name = "contigs") |>
  left_join(cv |> group_by(category) |> summarise(Mb = round(sum(len) / 1e6, 2),
                                                  samples = n_distinct(sample_id)), by = "category") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * contigs / sum(contigs), 1)) |>
  arrange(match(category, cats)) |> kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
tv |> count(virus_group, verdict = sub(" \\+.*", "", verdict), name = "taxa") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = virus_group, values_from = taxa, values_fill = 0) |>
  kable(caption = "Taxa by majority verdict")
```

All 711 taxa are in the searchable table below, and in `are_these_real/taxon_verdicts.tsv`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-all
#| code-summary: "Interactive table of every taxon"
DT::datatable(
  tv |> select(name, virus_group, family, n_contigs, n_samples, all_of(cats), genuine_samples,
               eve_samples, main_class, verdict),
  rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", extensions = "Buttons",
  options = list(pageLength = 25, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("csv"),
                 order = list(list(3, "desc"))))
```

<!-- CONCLUSIONS -->

# Files and versions

All intermediate files are in `are_these_real/`, beside this document. The extraction
outputs (`fasta/`, `blast/`, `ids/`, `summary.tsv`, `lca_assignments.tsv`, `extract.log`,
`viral_taxids.tsv`) are in this directory, and the analysis scripts are in `scripts/`.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `viral_taxa.tsv` | the 711 viral LCA taxa: lineage, virus group, counts |
| `allhits.tsv`, `contig_evidence.tsv` | every BLAST hit with subject organism group; per-contig nucleotide evidence |
| `all_viral.fa`, `allviraldb.*` | all contigs (sample-prefixed) and their BLAST db |
| `ncbi/hitrec.{fa,ft}`, `ncbi/hitrec_prot.fa` | viral records hit: sequence, feature tables, CDS proteins |
| `protdb_download/`, `protdb.fa`, `protdb_groups.tsv`, `protdb.dmnd` | competitive protein database |
| `diamond.tsv`, `protein_evidence.tsv` | raw DIAMOND blastx; per-contig protein call |
| `hits_ref.tsv`, `hotspots.tsv`, `hotspot_members.tsv` | viral hits on the references; hotspots and their contigs |
| `hotspot_windows.{fa,tsv}`, `elements.tsv`, `element_copies.tsv`, `E*.fa`, `E*_{up,down}*` | windows, elements, copies, flanks and clusters |
| `remote_blast.{json,tsv}` | NCBI BLAST of element probes (viruses excluded) |
| `reading_frames.tsv` | stops and frames of protein-supported contigs |
| **`contig_verdicts.tsv`** | **one row per contig: class and category** |
| **`taxon_verdicts.tsv`** | **one row per taxon: category counts and verdict** |

```{bash}
#| label: versions
#| code-summary: "Tool versions"
blastn -version | head -1; diamond version; cd-hit-est -h 2>&1 | head -1; seqkit version; python3 --version
```
